title: Introduce segmented-traffic-reservoir and staggered-rollout guard for noisy-neighbor mitigation
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds segmented traffic reservoir and staggered rollout guard to reduce false-positive regressions caused by noisy neighbor traffic slices. Backwards compatible; default policy enabled but configurable per-canary.
description: Motivation: We've seen an uptick in false-positive canary failures when small, high-latency traffic slices (noisy neighbors, churned tenants, spikey integration tests) distort global latency signals. Existing detectors treat traffic as a single stream which amplifies low-volume noise during gradual rollouts. This PR introduces two complementary mechanisms: (1) a segmented-traffic-reservoir that preserves per-slice baselines and provides representative sampling for low-volume segments, and (2) a staggered-rollout guard that phases weight increases across segments to avoid correlated blowups.
description_details: Design summary: 1) Segmented reservoir: maintains an independent reservoir sampler per traffic slice (routing key: tenant_id / route / region). Each reservoir tracks lightweight quantile sketch state (t-digest) and an EWMA of the 95th/99th percentiles. Reservoir sizes are proportional to slice entropy and capped to bound memory. 2) Adaptive threshold fabric: thresholds are computed per-slice using an EWMA of historical quantiles plus a multiplicative safety margin that shrinks as slice volume grows. 3) Staggered rollout guard: when a canary increases traffic weight, weight ramping is applied per-segment with jittered start times and configurable hold windows. The guard uses slice-level verdicts to compute a global canary decision via a weighted aggregation that downweights low-volume but highly-volatile slices.
implementation_notes: - New package perf_canary/reservoir adds SegmentReservoir and SegmentSampler (Rust -> native bindings). - Threshold fabric is implemented as policy nodes under perf_canary/detectors/fabric.rs. - Rollout guard implemented in perf_canary/guards/staggered_guard.{rs,py} and wired into the canary controller. - Console integration: exposes `canary.slice.*` metrics and a `per-segment breakdown` toggle in the Canaries dashboard. - Policy DSL: small additions to canary policy YAML: segment_reservoir:{enabled:true, base_size:512, volume_scale: 0.1}, staggered_ramp:{window_s:120, jitter_s:30, hold_s:300}
example_policy_snippet:
segment_reservoir:
  enabled: true
  base_size: 512
  volume_scale: 0.1
staggered_ramp:
  window_s: 120
  jitter_s: 30
  hold_s: 300

review_comments: Arjun Patel: Nice separation of concerns. Two questions: how do we bound worst-case memory if there are millions of slices? Is there a global eviction policy?

Maya Chen (reply): We cap reservoirs by configurable max_segments and use LRU eviction with a compacted sketch flush to long-term store. The default max_segments is conservative (50k) and we included telemetry to monitor evictions.
Sofia Martinez: The staggered ramp windows look right, but can we make hold_s configurable per-canary? Some customers want longer holds during large deploys.
Maya Chen (reply): Exposed hold_s in the policy DSL and added validation in the controller. Updated docs with example per-canary override.
Diego Alvarez: CI flaked on e2e due to clock skew in the test harness. Please add a clock tolerance in tests.
Maya Chen (reply): Added test harness tolerance and retried CI; included note in test file.
Arjun Patel: Approved after second pass. Marking for squash-merge.
merge: post-merge: applied migrations to canary policy store; rolling restart on controller downstream
testing_and_rollout: Testing: added unit tests for reservoir edge-cases (empty slices, single-sample slices), integration tests that simulate tenant noise and synthetic microbursts, and an e2e scenario that verifies gradual canary wins/rollbacks when a noisy slice spikes. Rollout: enabled behind feature flag perf.segmented_reservoir; staged rollout to 10% of clusters for 48h, monitor canary slice eviction and alerting. Monitoring: new metrics canary.slice.count, canary.slice.evictions, canary.slice.p95_ewma, and guard.staggered.*. Alerts suppressed for slices with volume < 50 req/min by default.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: new per-slice state could increase memory usage and introduce bookkeeping CPU. Mitigations: conservative defaults (base_size 512, max_segments 50k), LRU eviction, and a telemetry-driven kill-switch. We added a circuit-breaker that disables per-slice aggregation under controller memory pressure and falls back to legacy global detector.
